claims.text: Pulumi emits placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` when an Output<T> is treated as a plain value (e.g., string-interpolated) in a log line, generated file, or resource property.

A page titled 'Output value errors' exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ and covers this placeholder-text symptom and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud/CLI can produce the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when an update is already running on a stack.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs (architecture mismatch).
When the Pulumi CLI can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, it emits errors of the form read ".pulumi/meta.yaml".
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml.

The linked Pulumi docs pages (update-conflicts, server-errors, post-step-errors, connection-issues, destroy-failures, interrupted-updates, architecture-mismatch, output-values, CI/CD troubleshooting, editing-state-files, restoring-deleted-stacks, targeted-updates, logging, using-dev-builds) exist.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide has an #automatic-logging section covering `pulumi logs share`.
`pulumi destroy` can fail in some scenarios.
Pulumi Community Slack is available at slack.pulumi.com for community support.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
GitHub issue pulumi/pulumi#20846 relates to the new update conflict page redirect.
GitHub issue pulumi/docs#16985 relates to the new verbose logging page; the CLI verbose logging section is at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The docs pages 'Accessing single outputs with Apply' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/) and 'Working with multiple outputs' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/) exist.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ has an #outputs anchor.

When an output value is converted to a string directly (concatenated or logged) instead of via apply, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, interpolating an Output into a template string yields text containing `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string via f-string produces text containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the correct way to serialize an output to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In C#, interpolating an Output into a string yields text containing `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# (but not Go).

String-composition helpers for outputs: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript; `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, `Output.json_dumps` in Python; `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go; `Output.Format` in C#.
When an output is misused in string conversion, `pulumi up` still succeeds and the program runs.

A value read inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback; the apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned within it is still undefined when read afterward.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix the issue.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on an Output evaluates the output object itself and is generally always true regardless of the eventual value.
In statically typed languages, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name or using it as a loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, because these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/ has a #stackreferences anchor describing StackReference, which can consume another stack's outputs.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously extract a resolved value from an output; awaiting or reading synchronously either fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g., `res.Outputs` in Go).
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ exists.
